questions.explanation_english: (1) Reflexive relation – A relation R on set A is said to be reflexive if (a, a) is there in relation R ∀a ∈A. (2) Symmetric relation – A relation R on set is said to be symmetric if (a, b) is there in relation R then (b, a) should also be there in relation R ∀ a, b ∈ A. (3) Transitive relation – A relation R on set A is said to be transitive if (a, b) and (b, c) are there in the relation R then (a, c) should also be there in the relation R ∀ a, b, c ∈A. A relation is an equivalence relation if it is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Now, equivalence relations that can be defined on the set {4, 5, 6} are- (1) {(4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 6)} (2) {(4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 6), (4, 5), (5, 4)} (3) {(4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 6), (4, 6), (6, 4)} (4) {(4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 6), (5, 6), (6, 5)} (5) {(4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 6), (4, 5), (5, 4), (4, 6), (6, 4), (5, 6), (6, 5)} Thus number of equivalence relation is 5.
